- **Grays and blue-grays** throughout (hazy sky, dark performance shots)
- **Rust/orange-browns** appearing consistently (desert landscape)
- **Dark maroons/reddish-browns** (canyon walls in shadow)
- A few muted teal/dark blue stripes (bluish sky tones)
- A **light gray opening stripe** (the video famously begins with a bright, hazy sky shot before descending into the desert world)

This muted mix of rust-brown desert tones and gray sky is highly characteristic of the CGI desert landscape in Linkin Park's "In the End" video. The other candidates don't fit:
- "Zombie" would be almost purely black-and-white grays
- "Numb" would be monochromatic blue-gray (cathedral setting)
- "Hymn for the Weekend," "Sorry," and "Without Me" would be bright and saturated
- "Heathens" would be much darker with greenish prison tones
- "November Rain" would show a distinctly bright white cluster (the wedding scene)

The alternating gray (sky) and brown/rust (desert sand and rock) pattern across the whole timeline, with dark band performance shots interspersed, points to the desert CGI world of "In the End."

Answer: H
